macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Wall Street ends lower amid AI-spending and oil concerns
items.summary: U.S. stocks finished a volatile week lower as concerns over the cost and financing of artificial-intelligence investment weighed on technology shares, while rising oil prices renewed inflation concerns. The Dow fell 1.23% to 52,215.16, the S&P 500 declined 0.52% to 7,623.68, and the Nasdaq lost 0.21% to 25,955.34.

items.title: Fed expected to hold rates next week; December hike in focus
items.summary: Markets broadly expect the Federal Reserve to leave interest rates unchanged at its upcoming policy meeting, while investors are watching for signals about a possible quarter-point increase in December. U.S. Treasury yields rose, with the 10-year yield near 5.0%.

items.title: Oil rises above $100 as Middle East supply risks intensify
items.summary: Crude prices surged, with U.S. oil moving back above $100 a barrel and Brent reaching a six-month high as continued regional attacks raised concerns about disruptions to Middle East energy supplies. The increase intensified inflation and interest-rate worries.

items.title: U.S. activity remains firm but services growth slows
items.summary: October flash data showed U.S. services activity easing to 57.9 from 58.8, while manufacturing activity improved to a 53-month high of 56.0. Persistent cost pressures remained a concern for monetary policy and markets.

items.title: American Express raises outlook while announcing job cuts
items.summary: American Express raised its profit forecast but said it plans to eliminate 5% of its workforce. Its shares declined during Friday trading and weighed on the Dow.

items.title: SLB beats estimates as energy shares benefit from higher oil
items.summary: Oilfield-services provider SLB reported better-than-expected third-quarter profit, sending its shares up 7% as higher crude prices supported the energy sector.

items.title: Major technology earnings due next week
items.summary: Investors are preparing for results from Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon, with particular attention on their capital-spending plans and the profitability of large-scale AI investment. Roughly one-third of S&P 500 companies are expected to report quarterly results.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin and major cryptocurrencies retreat
items.summary: Bitcoin traded near $80,844, down about 1.2% over 24 hours, while Ethereum fell 1.4% to roughly $2,379. The global crypto market capitalization declined 1.1% to approximately $2.81 trillion, with Solana and XRP also lower.

items.title: Crypto liquidations surge as Bitcoin drops
items.summary: Crypto markets recorded about $336 million in liquidations over 24 hours, including $281 million in liquidated long positions. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs saw approximately $635 million in net outflows, reportedly their largest single-day outflow since late June.

items.title: Initia pauses blockchain after exploit
items.summary: Initia halted its layer-1 blockchain and associated rollups after a reported exploit enabled unauthorized token minting. Researchers estimated that more than $2.6 million in crypto assets had been drained.

items.title: SEC adds tokenization to examination priorities
items.summary: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission identified tokenization as an area of focus in its fiscal 2027 examination priorities, citing emerging market and infrastructure risks associated with tokenized securities.

items.title: Ethereum Glamsterdam testnet activation postponed
items.summary: Ethereum developers postponed the planned Glamsterdam upgrade activation on the Hoodi test network after ChainSecurity identified issues involving the upgrade’s gas-related changes.

items.title: OKX tokenized-stock plans face corporate objections
items.summary: Twenty-two listed companies, including Wells Fargo, Arm and Intuit, reportedly objected to plans for trading their shares on the OKX-ICE tokenized-stock platform, which had planned to list 63 stocks.

items.title: Utexo opens early access for Bitcoin-based USDT product
items.summary: Tether-backed Utexo opened early access to Utexo Mint, a version of USDT designed for the Bitcoin network, ahead of a planned November 28 launch.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Moonshot AI launches Kimi K3.1 Pro with cyber-safety limits
items.summary: Moonshot AI unveiled Kimi K3.1 Pro, a roughly 3-trillion-parameter-class open-weight model with a 1-million-token context window. The company reduced its cyber-offensive capabilities amid concerns about AI-assisted hacking and plans to release the full weights in November.[2]

items.title: OpenAI resumes frontier-model training after security overhaul
items.summary: OpenAI resumed training its most advanced models after pausing work following an incident in which a research model gained limited internet access through a configuration error. The company said it strengthened isolation measures and fixed a vulnerability in the Brotli compression software.[7]

items.title: Canva releases Craft image-generation model
items.summary: Canva launched Craft, an in-house image model designed to plan spatial relationships before rendering images. It supports outputs up to 2K resolution across 30 aspect ratios and is available through Dream Lab and the Canva API.[3]

items.title: NVIDIA releases Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B for local AI
items.summary: NVIDIA introduced Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B, an open small language model designed for local voice assistants, game characters and robots. It targets systems with about 4 GB of VRAM, including RTX PCs and Jetson devices.[3]

items.title: Block unveils Dessa speech-to-speech model
items.summary: Block announced Dessa, a full-duplex speech-to-speech model trained from scratch on human conversation audio rather than text or pretrained models. The system is designed to listen and speak simultaneously while modeling conversational timing, emotion and laughter.[9]

items.title: DeepSeek releases V4.1-Flash-1017 open-weight model
items.summary: DeepSeek released V4.1-Flash-1017, claiming improvements in coding benchmark performance, task speed and output efficiency compared with its predecessor. The model’s weights were published openly.[5]

items.title: EU publishes first AI Act harmonised standard
items.summary: The European Commission published a reference to EN 18286:2026, the first harmonised standard supporting the EU AI Act’s quality-management requirements. Providers of covered high-risk systems implementing the standard receive a presumption of conformity for the provisions it addresses.[5]

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: AI copycat games spark developer fears in South Korea
items.summary: At least seven Roblox games reportedly appeared within a day of a demo video, closely copying its mechanics. South Korean studios have canceled or restricted demo releases amid concerns that AI tools are making cloning faster and harder to prevent.

items.title: Electronic Arts reportedly cuts about 400 jobs as BioWare closes
items.summary: Electronic Arts is reported to be reducing its global workforce by roughly 400 employees while closing BioWare, the studio associated with Mass Effect, Dragon Age, and Baldur’s Gate. Reports say the Mass Effect franchise will continue despite the studio’s closure.

items.title: Sashi owner accuses Valve of preferential treatment in CS2 dispute
items.summary: Sashi’s owner accused Valve of favoring BC.Game over regional roster-swap rules after Sashi parted ways with TjP and Hatz. The dispute has also prompted discussion about Valve’s handling of competitive Counter-Strike governance.

items.title: FIFAe Finals postponed indefinitely
items.summary: The 2026 FIFAe Finals have been postponed until further notice because of regional security developments, including ongoing Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia.

items.title: Esports World Cup announces 2027 qualifier program
items.summary: The Esports World Cup announced a program allowing more tournament organizers and local esports communities to stage official qualifying events on the route to the 2027 competition.

items.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 launches worldwide
items.summary: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 reportedly released globally, introducing a campaign set in Korea, the Kill Block mode, and the return of DMZ.

items.title: Final Fantasy Resonance releases across major platforms
items.summary: Final Fantasy Resonance became available on October 22 for PC, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, Nintendo Switch, and Nintendo Switch 2.

items.title: US video game market stabilizes in September
items.summary: Circana data cited by GamesMarket put US video game industry revenue at $4.76 billion in September, slightly below the prior year, while hardware and accessory sales reportedly returned to year-over-year growth.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: Apple’s iPhone Duo foldable launches amid global shortages
items.summary: Apple’s first foldable iPhone reportedly went on sale worldwide on October 23 and quickly sold out in stores, with strong demand pushing shipping estimates into January. The device is priced from approximately $2,000.

items.title: SpaceX reportedly seeks access to 80,000 U.S. cell sites
items.summary: SpaceX is reportedly negotiating agreements with cellular infrastructure companies to access at least 80,000 sites across the United States, supporting plans to expand Starlink Mobile and establish a major wireless carrier.

items.title: Critical PHP vulnerability prompts widespread emergency patching
items.summary: A serious vulnerability in widely used PHP software has triggered urgent patching by websites and organizations, with reports describing temporary outages as operators worked to secure affected systems.
